diagnosis: Osteoblastic bone metastases from prostate cancer
symptom: a dull lower back ache blamed on an old mattress
hook: One vertebra turned to solid chalk among its grey neighbours.
whatYouSee: One lumbar vertebra glows solid white with dense round white spots scattered through the right side of the patient's pelvis.
whyItMatters: Prostate cancer spreads to bone as dense osteoblastic deposits in the pelvis and lumbar spine. Large or poorly differentiated tumours are the ones more often metastatic.
treatment: If bone metastases are suspected the workup includes PSA, biopsy, and a bone scan. Treatment then depends on the stage of the disease.
takeaway: A white ivory vertebra in an older man should make you think of prostate cancer.

defects: Unexplained additional image findings: ["The independent read identifies the calcifications as soft-tissue chondroid-pattern calcifications overlying the right iliac fossa rather than intraosseous sclerotic blobs; the morphology described (lobulated 'popcorn' pattern without cortical involvement) raises the possibility of a soft-tissue chondroid lesion rather than purely intraosseous osteoblastic metastases, but this is a projection-ambiguity that cannot be resolved from the plain film alone and does not constitute an additional unrelated lesion","The lumbar disc space narrowing and endplate sclerosis at L4-L5 and L5-S1 noted by the independent read is a degenerative change incidental to the stated diagnosis; dense sclerosis at L5-S1 could represent an additional metastatic focus not explicitly named in the expected findings — this requires flagging as an unexplained finding relative to the stated pattern which specifies L4 ivory vertebra and S1 upper sacrum density only"]

findings: AP projection pelvis and lower lumbar spine radiograph
Multiple discrete, rounded, densely calcified foci of varying sizes clustered within the right iliac wing/right iliac fossa region, with a 'popcorn' or lobulated calcification pattern
The calcifications are confined to the soft tissues overlying the right iliac bone and do not appear to arise from the bone cortex itself
Lumbar spine shows multilevel disc space narrowing with endplate sclerosis and osteophyte formation, most pronounced at L4-L5 and L5-S1
Dense sclerosis at the L5-S1 level with apparent loss of disc height
Bilateral hip joints appear preserved without obvious joint space narrowing
No obvious periosteal reaction or cortical destruction of the right iliac wing underlying the calcifications
Bowel gas pattern is unremarkable on this limited view
No radio-opaque urinary calculi identified in the visualised ureters or bladder region
differential: Soft tissue chondroid neoplasm with dystrophic calcification in the right iliac fossa (e.g., soft tissue chondroma or chondrosarcoma) — the lobulated 'popcorn' calcification pattern is characteristic of chondroid matrix
Synovial chondromatosis or calcific deposits within a bursa or soft tissue mass overlying the right iliac region

Multiple phleboliths or dystrophic calcifications within a soft tissue vascular malformation (e.g., venous malformation) in the right iliac fossa — though the calcification morphology appears more lobulated/chondroid than typical phlebolith rings
anatomyConcerns: The clustering and morphology of the right-sided calcifications are distinctly abnormal and represent true pathology rather than normal anatomical structure
Mild rotational asymmetry of the pelvis on this projection may slightly affect assessment of the sacroiliac joints
The upper lumbar and lower thoracic spine are partially excluded from the field of view, limiting full spinal assessment
